FINAL HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded):

Diversity in Pottery Form collapsed while Diversity in Pottery Decoration increased simultaneously in the 18th century BCE (BCE 1800–1701), the change being first registered at the 1700 BCE grid point (i.e., CE −1700). In that single 100-year window, Pottery Form diversity Z dropped from +0.74 (1800 BCE) to −1.13 (1700 BCE), Δ = −1.87 — the largest one-century Form decline in the entire record (second largest is only −0.90) — while Pottery Decoration diversity Z rose from −0.48 to +0.97, Δ = +1.45, in the same century. This is the only century in which Form collapses and Decoration increases simultaneously. The new state persisted for the rest of the record: Form Z is pinned at −1.13 from 1700 through 500 BCE, and Decoration Z stays elevated at 0.97 (until 1100 BCE) and then 1.53 (from 1000 BCE onward). Expressed either way — as the century interval (18th century BCE, BCE 1800–1701) or as the first new-state grid value (1700 BCE / CE −1700) — the answer identifies the same event.

payload.hypothesis: Diversity in Pottery Form collapsed while Diversity in Pottery Decoration increased simultaneously in the 18th century BCE (BCE 1800-1701; first registered at 1700 BCE / CE -1700): PotteryForm Z 0.74 -> -1.13 (delta -1.87, largest single-century drop in record) and PotteryDecoration Z -0.48 -> 0.97 (delta +1.45) in the same 100-year window; the only such simultaneous century, with a persistent post-event plateau (Form -1.13 through 500 BCE; Decoration 0.97 then 1.53).
payload.workflow: 1) Inspected 3 datasets: time_series_data.csv (annual CE -4100..-500; PotteryForm/PotteryDecoration sparse centennial raw + fully interpolated _inter), capital.csv (BCE 4300..500 centennial grid; ZKeform=PotteryForm, Zkeverz=PotteryDecoration, German decimal commas; period groups EN/MN/SG/LN/OBA/YBA), pollen file (auxiliary, no pottery data; calBP/CE offset inconsistent). 2) Cross-validated capital.csv vs time_series_data.csv pottery indices: max abs diff = 0.0 over 37 matched centuries -> identical, used capital.csv BCE grid as canonical. 3) Computed per-century changes (oldest->newest): identified the unique strict same-century step BCE 1800->1700 with dForm=-1.87 and dDec=+1.45. 4) Sensitivity checks: magnitude thresholds (|dForm|>0.5..1.5, dDec>=0.5..1.0 all give the same single step; threshold 2.0 removes all), +-1-century overlap (band of centers 1400..2000 BCE all capture the same event), and corroboration via annual interpolated series (only 100-y window 1800->1700 has Form collapse + Decoration rise). 5) Persistence: collapsed Form (-1.13) and elevated Decoration (0.97 -> 1.53) sustained for all subsequent centuries. Final: 18th century BCE (BCE 1800-1701), first new-state grid value 1700 BCE (CE -1700).
payload.candidate_century: 18th century BCE (BCE 1800-1701); grid value 1700 BCE / CE -1700
